channel.description: Alertas de vulnerabilidade (CVSS) - fonte NVD (fallback quando o SecurityWizardry está bloqueado) - RMFconsultoria

item.title: CVE-2026-126662 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | Contao 4.0.0 before 5.3.54, 5.4.0 before 5.7.17, and 6.0.0 before 6.0.6 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows filemount-restricted backend users to modify folders outside their filemount via the file manager Edit-Multiple operation. Attackers holding the protected or syncExclude field permission can submit outside folder paths in the IDS parameter to publish protected folders or exclude them from DBAFS synchronization, exposing files for public download.

item.title: CVE-2026-126663 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | Contao 4.0.0 before 5.3.54, 5.4.0 before 5.7.17, and 6.0.0 before 6.0.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows content editors to read image files anywhere on the filesystem via the {{image::}} insert tag. Attackers can embed percent-encoded sequences like ..%2f that pass Validator::isInsecurePath() before rawurldecode(), making the frontend resize and serve readable image files outside the files directory.

item.title: CVE-2026-94125 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | Nimbus returns the worker placement of every topology running on a supervisor, including the host, port, owner and resource assignment of topologies the caller is not authorized to read. In a multi-tenant cluster, an authenticated user who is allowed to access Nimbus can learn where the workers of other users' topologies run. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.0, which fixes the issue.

item.title: CVE-2026-124746 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.5
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.5 | A flaw was found in BusyBox. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted filesystem image on an attached storage device. When probed by utilities such as blkid, findfs, or mount, the application crashes, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) that prevents the system from resolving or mounting storage devices.
